memories.content: Define in one sentence the user groups and usage contexts to which the design knowledge does not apply.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through explicitly excluded targets and situations.
Specify user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints under which the proposed design knowledge can be transferred.
Small-scale formative studies can support analytic generalization distinct from statistical representativeness when results are expressed in terms of design conditions and mechanisms.
The author of this proposal tends to apply design knowledge derived from an accessible sample to a broader user population.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The reference frame focuses on transfer boundaries, analytic generalization, and overextension from accessible samples. The compared frame independently addresses terminology, abbreviations, operational-role clarity, site-dependent permissions, and collapsing distinct roles under “user.” No substantive overlap or scope-aligned disagreement is established.

relations.reason: The instruction to state exclusions and the account of how reviewers use them express complementary parts of one reference-only claim about defining applicability boundaries.
relations.summary: Explicitly excluded users and situations establish the boundary of generalization.

relations.reason: This independently specifies the positive conditions under which design knowledge may transfer and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Transferability should be stated through user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only methodological claim about the basis and limits of generalization.
relations.summary: Small formative studies may support analytic generalization through design conditions and mechanisms without statistical representativeness.

relations.reason: This reference-only observation identifies a specific overgeneralization tendency rather than prescribing transfer boundaries or terminology.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to extend knowledge from an accessible sample to a broader population.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only rule about terminological continuity.
relations.summary: Names for the same roles, functions, and stages should remain consistent throughout the proposal.

relations.reason: This compared-only rule governs whether abbreviation is warranted, independently of first-use definition.
relations.summary: In a two-page proposal, abbreviations should be reserved for long recurring terms.

relations.reason: The first-use rule and the reviewer-comprehension observation form one compared-only claim and its rationale.
relations.summary: An abbreviation should be paired with its full term at first use because context alone may not make it clear across subfields.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only naming principle for participants.
relations.summary: Study participants should be named by the roles they perform rather than by status.

relations.reason: This compared-only requirement concerns the substantive definition of roles, not merely their labels.
relations.summary: A newly introduced operational role should be defined by both its decisions and its actions.

relations.reason: This compared-only observation identifies deployment site as a source of operational variation among nominally identical roles.
relations.summary: Identical job titles may conceal site-dependent differences in modification privileges and data access.

relations.reason: This compared-only observation identifies a specific role-collapsing tendency.
relations.summary: The user tends to collapse distinct field roles into the single label “user.”

reports.compared_only: The compared frame promotes stable, role-based terminology; disciplined abbreviation use; explicit role definitions; attention to site-specific permissions; and avoidance of collapsing distinct roles into “user.”
reports.reference_only: The reference addresses exclusions and transfer conditions, distinguishes analytic from statistical generalization, and flags overextension from accessible samples.
